title: The Witcher Franchise Overview
body:
The Witcher began as short stories and novels by Polish author Andrzej Sapkowski, published from the late 1980s in magazines and from 1992 in book form, and later grew into video games and a television series documented in public release records.

This public edition records only verifiable facts — book titles, authors, publication years and game release years — in original wording, with no copied passages, dialogue or game text.

The companion Signature edition is separate, labeled unofficial fiction with original monster-hunters and villages, and it claims no affiliation with or endorsement by the rights holders.

How to use this record: start with the overview, then read the work-by-work records in publication order. Every date and credit below is a public fact; no copyrighted text is reproduced anywhere in this database.

title: The Witcher Reading and Viewing Order Guide
body:
Recommended public order for the works in this database is publication and release order, beginning with Sword of Destiny (Polish book edition) (1992) and ending with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015). That order follows how the franchise actually reached the public, and it avoids assuming any later reordering.

The full order is: Sword of Destiny (Polish book edition) (1992); The Last Wish (Polish book edition) (1993); Blood of Elves (1994); Time of Contempt (1995); Baptism of Fire (1996); The Tower of the Swallow (1997); The Lady of the Lake (1999); The Witcher (video game) (2007); Season of Storms (2013); The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015). Each title in that list has its own record in this database with its credited creators and format.

This guide contains facts only. It does not reproduce story text, and it does not claim that any Signature continuation belongs in the official order.
